index.html.name: Is CreditStud.io free to use?
index.html.acceptedAnswer: Yes, all our calculators and tools are completely free. We earn affiliate commissions when you apply for cards through our site, but this never affects our rankings — those are based purely on math.

index.html.name: Does using the calculator affect my credit score?
index.html.acceptedAnswer: No. Our calculators are just math — no credit checks, no personal data collected, no impact on your score whatsoever.

index.html.name: How accurate are the results?
index.html.acceptedAnswer: We use publicly available APR, fee, and reward data updated monthly. Results reflect current terms, but actual offers may vary by credit profile.

index.html.name: What's the difference between the calculators?
index.html.acceptedAnswer: Credit Comparison finds the cheapest way to finance a specific purchase. Debt Planner helps you pay off existing debt faster. Rewards Calculator finds the best credit card for your spending habits.

min-payment/index.html.name: How long does it take to pay off a credit card making only minimum payments?
min-payment/index.html.acceptedAnswer: It depends on your balance and APR, but it can take decades. For example, a $5,000 balance at 24.99% APR with a 2% minimum payment would take over 32 years to pay off and cost more than $11,000 in interest — you'd pay over 3x your original balance.

min-payment/index.html.name: How are minimum payments calculated?
min-payment/index.html.acceptedAnswer: Most issuers calculate minimum payments as a percentage of your balance (typically 1-3%), plus interest and fees, with a floor of $25-35. Some use a flat percentage; others use a tiered approach. Check your card agreement for the exact formula.

min-payment/index.html.name: What happens if I only pay the minimum on my credit card?
min-payment/index.html.acceptedAnswer: You'll stay in debt much longer and pay far more in interest. Minimum payments are designed to keep you paying — not to get you out of debt. Your credit utilization also stays high, which can hurt your credit score.

min-payment/index.html.name: How much money can I save by paying more than the minimum?
min-payment/index.html.acceptedAnswer: Even small increases make a huge difference. Adding just $25/month to a $5,000 balance at 25% APR can shave years off your payoff time and save thousands in interest. Adding $100/month can cut decades down to a few years.

min-payment/index.html.name: Should I get a balance transfer card to escape the minimum payment trap?
min-payment/index.html.acceptedAnswer: A 0% balance transfer card can be a powerful tool if you can pay off the balance during the intro period (typically 12-21 months). The 3-5% transfer fee is usually much less than the interest you'd pay on your current card. Just be sure to avoid running up new debt.

debt-planner/index.html.name: What is the debt snowball method?
debt-planner/index.html.acceptedAnswer: The debt snowball method, popularized by Dave Ramsey, involves paying minimum payments on all debts while putting any extra money toward your smallest balance first. Once that debt is paid off, you roll its payment amount into the next smallest balance, creating a 'snowball' effect. This method is psychologically motivating because you see quick wins.

debt-planner/index.html.name: What is the debt avalanche method?
debt-planner/index.html.acceptedAnswer: The debt avalanche method (also called debt stacking) involves paying minimums on all debts while directing extra payments to the debt with the highest interest rate first. Once that's paid off, you move to the next highest rate. This is mathematically optimal and saves the most money on interest over time.

debt-planner/index.html.name: Which is better: debt snowball or debt avalanche?
debt-planner/index.html.acceptedAnswer: The avalanche method saves more money on interest, while the snowball method provides quicker psychological wins. Research shows the best method is the one you'll actually stick with. If you need motivation, try snowball. If you're disciplined and want to minimize cost, try avalanche.

debt-planner/index.html.name: How do I calculate my debt-free date?
debt-planner/index.html.acceptedAnswer: To calculate your debt-free date, list all debts with their balances, interest rates, and minimum payments. Then simulate paying them off month by month, applying extra payments according to your chosen strategy (snowball or avalanche). Our free Debt Payoff Planner does this calculation instantly and shows you exactly when you'll be debt-free.

debt-planner/index.html.name: Should I pay off debt or invest?
debt-planner/index.html.acceptedAnswer: If your debt interest rate is above 7-8%, paying it off first usually makes more sense than investing. High-interest credit card debt (15-25% APR) is essentially a guaranteed return when you pay it down. For lower-rate debt like mortgages, investing may yield better returns. Use our planner to see exactly how much interest you'll save with extra payments.

loan-vs-bt/index.html.name: Is a personal loan or balance transfer better for paying off credit card debt?
loan-vs-bt/index.html.acceptedAnswer: It depends on your debt amount, payoff timeline, and credit score. Balance transfers are best for smaller debts ($10-15k) you can pay off during the 0% intro period. Personal loans work better for larger debts, longer timelines, or if you prefer fixed monthly payments. Use our calculator to compare your actual costs.

loan-vs-bt/index.html.name: What are the risks of a balance transfer?
loan-vs-bt/index.html.acceptedAnswer: The main risk is not paying off the balance during the intro period. After 0% APR expires (typically 12-21 months), the regular APR kicks in — often 18-29%. Balance transfer fees (3-5%) also add to the cost. Missing a payment can void the 0% offer entirely.

loan-vs-bt/index.html.name: What are origination fees on personal loans?
loan-vs-bt/index.html.acceptedAnswer: Origination fees are one-time charges (1-8% of the loan amount) deducted from your loan proceeds. For example, a $10,000 loan with a 5% origination fee means you receive $9,500 but repay $10,000 plus interest. Not all lenders charge them.

loan-vs-bt/index.html.name: Can I get a balance transfer with fair credit?
loan-vs-bt/index.html.acceptedAnswer: Most 0% balance transfer cards require good to excellent credit (670+). With fair credit (580-669), your options are limited. Capital One Quicksilver and some Discover cards may approve fair-credit applicants. Personal loans may be easier to qualify for with fair credit, though at higher rates.

loan-vs-bt/index.html.name: How much can I transfer to a balance transfer card?
loan-vs-bt/index.html.acceptedAnswer: You can transfer up to the credit limit you're approved for, minus any fees. Most people get limits of $5,000-$15,000. If your debt exceeds the limit, you'll need to keep the remainder on your old card or use a personal loan for the full amount.

learn/crypto-credit-card-rewards.html.name: Are crypto credit card rewards better than cash back?
learn/crypto-credit-card-rewards.html.acceptedAnswer: Crypto rewards can potentially grow in value, unlike fixed cash back. However, they come with volatility risk, tax complexity, and potential conversion fees. Cash back is simpler, more predictable, and easier to budget with. For most users, cash back cards offer steadier utility with less complexity.

learn/crypto-credit-card-rewards.html.name: How do crypto credit card rewards work?
learn/crypto-credit-card-rewards.html.acceptedAnswer: Each purchase earns a percentage of cryptocurrency (Bitcoin, Ethereum, etc.) based on the dollar amount spent. Rewards are typically deposited to your crypto wallet or exchange account associated with the card. Rates range from 1-5%, with some premium cards offering higher rates on specific categories.

learn/crypto-credit-card-rewards.html.name: What are the tax implications of crypto credit card rewards?
learn/crypto-credit-card-rewards.html.acceptedAnswer: Crypto rewards are generally taxable as ordinary income at their fair market value when received. This adds complexity to your tax filing, as you must track the value of each reward earned throughout the year. Consult a tax professional familiar with cryptocurrency for advice specific to your situation.

learn/crypto-credit-card-rewards.html.name: Do crypto credit cards charge foreign transaction fees?
learn/crypto-credit-card-rewards.html.acceptedAnswer: Most crypto credit cards waive foreign transaction fees, making them suitable for international travel. However, always verify this feature before traveling, as some cards may charge 1-3% fees on foreign transactions.

learn/crypto-credit-card-rewards.html.name: Which crypto credit card has the best rewards?
learn/crypto-credit-card-rewards.html.acceptedAnswer: The 'best' card depends on your spending patterns and crypto preferences. Popular options include the Gemini credit card (up to 4% crypto rewards), Crypto.com cards (up to 5% depending on tier), and BlockFi credit card (1.5-3.5% rewards). Compare annual fees, reward rates, and crypto options using our calculator.

learn/crypto-credit-card-rewards.html.name: How do I calculate the value of crypto credit card rewards?
learn/crypto-credit-card-rewards.html.acceptedAnswer: Our crypto rewards calculator factors in your monthly spending, reward rate, current crypto prices, and potential appreciation/depreciation over time. It compares crypto rewards against traditional cash back cards to show which offers better long-term value based on your assumptions about crypto price movements.

learn/crypto-credit-card-rewards.html.name: Are crypto credit cards safe to use?
learn/crypto-credit-card-rewards.html.acceptedAnswer: Major crypto credit cards are issued by established banks and offer the same fraud protection as traditional cards. However, crypto rewards introduce additional risks including price volatility, exchange security, and regulatory uncertainty. Only use reputable cards from established companies and secure wallets for storing rewards.

Once that debt is paid off, you roll its payment amount into the next smallest balance, creating a 'snowball' effect. This method is psychologically motivating because you see quick wins.

learn/snowball-vs-avalanche.html.name: How much money can I save with the debt avalanche method?
learn/snowball-vs-avalanche.html.acceptedAnswer: Savings depend on your specific debts, but the avalanche method can save hundreds or thousands of dollars in interest compared to snowball. For example, with debts totaling $15,000 at rates from 15-25%, avalanche might save $1,000-2,000 over the life of the debt. Our calculator shows your exact savings.

learn/snowball-vs-avalanche.html.name: How long does it take to pay off debt using snowball vs avalanche?
learn/snowball-vs-avalanche.html.acceptedAnswer: Both methods take the same amount of time if you make identical monthly payments. The difference is in the order of debt elimination. Snowball gives you faster early wins (smaller balances disappear first), while avalanche reduces your total interest cost throughout the process.

learn/snowball-vs-avalanche.html.name: How do I decide between debt snowball and avalanche methods?
learn/snowball-vs-avalanche.html.acceptedAnswer: Our debt payoff calculator compares both methods side-by-side using your actual debts, interest rates, and monthly payment. It shows the total time, interest savings, and psychological factors to help you choose the approach that best fits your personality and financial goals.

learn/snowball-vs-avalanche.html.name: Can I combine snowball and avalanche methods?
learn/snowball-vs-avalanche.html.acceptedAnswer: Yes! Some people start with snowball to build momentum, then switch to avalanche once they're committed to the process. Others use snowball for smaller debts and avalanche for larger ones. The key is consistency - pick a method and stick with it rather than constantly switching approaches.

learn/balance-transfer-calculator.html.name: How much can I save with a balance transfer?
learn/balance-transfer-calculator.html.acceptedAnswer: Transferring a $10,000 balance from a 22.99% APR card to a 0% APR card for 18 months can save $2,000+ in interest. Just watch out for 3-5% transfer fees ($300-500) and ensure you pay off the balance before the promo ends.

learn/balance-transfer-calculator.html.name: What is a good balance transfer offer?
learn/balance-transfer-calculator.html.acceptedAnswer: Look for cards with: 1) Long 0% intro APR periods (18-21 months), 2) Low or no balance transfer fees (0-3%), 3) No annual fee, 4) Reasonable regular APR after the intro period (under 20%), 5) Compatible credit score requirements. Our calculator helps you compare offers side-by-side.

learn/balance-transfer-calculator.html.name: How do balance transfer fees work?
learn/balance-transfer-calculator.html.acceptedAnswer: Most cards charge 3-5% of the transferred amount as a fee. For a $10,000 transfer, that's $300-500. Some cards offer promotional 0% transfer fees for limited time. Calculate whether the interest savings outweigh the transfer fee using our balance transfer calculator.

learn/balance-transfer-calculator.html.name: What happens after the 0% APR period ends?
learn/balance-transfer-calculator.html.acceptedAnswer: Any remaining balance will be subject to the regular purchase APR, typically 17-27%. If you haven't paid off the transferred balance, you'll start accruing interest at this higher rate. Our calculator shows your remaining balance at the end of the intro period so you can plan accordingly.

learn/balance-transfer-calculator.html.name: Can I transfer balances between cards from the same bank?
learn/balance-transfer-calculator.html.acceptedAnswer: Generally no - most banks don't allow balance transfers between their own cards. You'll need to transfer between cards from different issuers. Check with your specific bank for their policies.

learn/balance-transfer-calculator.html.name: How do I calculate if a balance transfer is worth it?
learn/balance-transfer-calculator.html.acceptedAnswer: Our 0% APR balance transfer calculator compares your current card's interest costs against the new card's transfer fee and post-promo interest. It shows your break-even point and net savings over time, factoring in your monthly payment amount and the length of the 0% APR offer.

learn/balance-transfer-calculator.html.name: What credit score do I need for the best balance transfer cards?
learn/balance-transfer-calculator.html.acceptedAnswer: The best 0% APR balance transfer offers typically require good to excellent credit (670+). Some cards offer shorter 0% periods for fair credit (630-669). If your score is lower, focus on improving it before applying, as multiple hard inquiries can further damage your score.

learn/bnpl-interest-calculator.html.name: Is BNPL worse than a credit card?
learn/bnpl-interest-calculator.html.acceptedAnswer: BNPL services typically have 0% interest rates but charge late fees ($7-68) and sometimes service fees. Credit cards have higher interest rates (15-25% APR) but offer stronger consumer protections, rewards, and credit building. For disciplined users who pay on time, BNPL can be cheaper. For those who carry balances, credit cards may be more flexible.

learn/bnpl-interest-calculator.html.name: What happens if I miss a BNPL payment?
learn/bnpl-interest-calculator.html.acceptedAnswer: Late fees vary by service: Klarna charges $7+, Afterpay charges $10 initially then $7 weekly up to $68 or 25% of purchase. Some services freeze accounts for missed payments. Unlike credit cards, BNPL services typically don't report on-time payments to credit bureaus, but they do report delinquencies.

learn/bnpl-interest-calculator.html.name: Do BNPL services affect my credit score?
learn/bnpl-interest-calculator.html.acceptedAnswer: Most BNPL services perform soft credit pulls that don't impact your score. Klarna and Affirm report to credit bureaus, potentially helping or hurting your score. Other services like Afterpay and PayPal Pay in 4 generally don't report, so on-time payments won't help your score but missed payments won't hurt it either.

learn/bnpl-interest-calculator.html.name: Which BNPL service is the cheapest?
learn/bnpl-interest-calculator.html.acceptedAnswer: PayPal Pay in 4 and Affirm Pay in 4 are the cheapest with 0% interest and no fees. Afterpay charges no fees but has steep late fees. Klarna charges small service fees ($0.75-3.00) plus late fees. Zip charges upfront origination fees equivalent to 30-35% APR, making it the most expensive option.

learn/bnpl-interest-calculator.html.name: Can I use BNPL for any purchase?
learn/bnpl-interest-calculator.html.acceptedAnswer: Availability varies by service. Klarna and Affirm offer virtual cards usable anywhere online. Afterpay and Zip work at partner merchants plus offer physical cards for in-store use. PayPal Pay in 4 is limited to online merchants with PayPal checkout integration. Always check if your retailer accepts your preferred BNPL service.

learn/bnpl-interest-calculator.html.name: How do I calculate the true cost of using BNPL services?
learn/bnpl-interest-calculator.html.acceptedAnswer: Our BNPL interest calculator factors in purchase amount, payment schedule, potential late fees, and service fees to show the total cost of your purchase. It compares different BNPL services side-by-side so you can choose the most cost-effective option.

learn/bnpl-interest-calculator.html.name: What are the interest rates for BNPL services?
learn/bnpl-interest-calculator.html.acceptedAnswer: While most BNPL services advertise 0% interest, some longer-term plans charge interest rates up to 36%. Affirm offers both interest-free options and longer-term plans with rates up to 36%. Klarna also offers financing options with similar rates. Always check the terms before agreeing to a payment plan.

learn/pay-off-10k-debt.html.name: How long does it take to pay off $10,000 in credit card debt?
learn/pay-off-10k-debt.html.acceptedAnswer: With minimum payments only, it could take 20+ years and cost over $15,000 in interest. With an extra $300-500 monthly payment, you can be debt-free in 2-3 years. Our debt planner shows your exact timeline.

learn/pay-off-10k-debt.html.name: What's the minimum payment on a $10,000 credit card?
learn/pay-off-10k-debt.html.acceptedAnswer: Most credit cards require 2-3% of the balance as minimum payment, meaning $200-300 monthly for a $10,000 balance. However, this approach extends payoff time dramatically and costs thousands in interest.

learn/pay-off-10k-debt.html.name: Is it better to pay off my smallest or highest interest credit card first?
learn/pay-off-10k-debt.html.acceptedAnswer: Mathematically, the debt avalanche (highest interest first) saves more money. Psychologically, the debt snowball (smallest balance first) builds momentum. Choose based on what keeps you motivated long-term.

learn/pay-off-10k-debt.html.name: How much can I save with a balance transfer for $10,000 debt?
learn/pay-off-10k-debt.html.acceptedAnswer: Transferring a $10,000 balance from a 22.99% APR card to a 0% APR card for 18 months can save $2,000+ in interest. Just watch out for 3-5% transfer fees ($300-500) and ensure you pay off the balance before the promo ends.

learn/pay-off-10k-debt.html.name: Should I consolidate $10,000 credit card debt with a personal loan?
learn/pay-off-10k-debt.html.acceptedAnswer: If you qualify for a personal loan with a lower interest rate than your credit cards, consolidation can simplify payments and reduce interest costs. However, you'll lose the flexibility of credit cards and face fixed monthly payments.

learn/pay-off-10k-debt.html.name: What are the fastest ways to pay off $10,000 in credit card debt?
learn/pay-off-10k-debt.html.acceptedAnswer: The fastest approaches include: 1) The debt avalanche method (pay minimums on all cards, extra toward highest interest), 2) Balance transfer to a 0% APR card, 3) Personal loan consolidation, 4) Increasing monthly payments by $300-500, 5) Cutting expenses to free up more payment money, 6) Taking on side income specifically for debt payoff.

learn/pay-off-10k-debt.html.name: How can I calculate how long it will take to pay off $10,000 in credit card debt?
learn/pay-off-10k-debt.html.acceptedAnswer: Our debt payoff calculator factors in your current balance, interest rate, and monthly payment to show your exact payoff timeline. It compares different strategies side-by-side so you can see which approach gets you debt-free fastest.

cards/capital-one-venture-x/index.html.name: Is the Venture X really only $395/year?
cards/capital-one-venture-x/index.html.acceptedAnswer: Effectively, no. After the $300 travel credit and 10K anniversary miles ($100), the net AF is ~$0/yr if you book any travel through Capital One Travel. It's the cheapest premium card available.

cards/capital-one-venture-x/index.html.name: How does the Venture X compare to Chase Sapphire Reserve and Amex Platinum?
cards/capital-one-venture-x/index.html.acceptedAnswer: Venture X is $150–$300 cheaper than Reserve/Platinum and includes lounge access, but transfer partners are weaker (no Hyatt, no Delta) and the travel portal can be pricier than booking direct.

cards/capital-one-venture-x/index.html.name: Are Capital One miles worth it?
cards/capital-one-venture-x/index.html.acceptedAnswer: Best value at 1.85¢+ via transfer partners (Air Canada Aeroplan, Avianca LifeMiles, Turkish Airlines). At 1¢ for "purchase eraser" they're mediocre; you need to learn transfer partners.

cards/capital-one-venture-x/index.html.name: Can I add authorized users for free?
cards/capital-one-venture-x/index.html.acceptedAnswer: Yes. Authorized users get full Priority Pass and Capital One Lounge access — that alone is worth ~$700/yr if your spouse travels with you.

cards/capital-one-venture-x/index.html.name: What's the catch with the $300 travel credit?
cards/capital-one-venture-x/index.html.acceptedAnswer: Must book through Capital One Travel portal. Prices are sometimes 3–10% higher than booking direct, so the credit's real value is closer to $250–$280 if you'd normally book elsewhere.

cards/capital-one-venture-x/index.html.name: Is the Venture X hard to get approved for?
cards/capital-one-venture-x/index.html.acceptedAnswer: Yes — Capital One is conservative. You'll typically need a 740+ FICO, low utilization, and clean recent inquiries. They also auto-decline applicants with too many recent Capital One products.

cards/citi-custom-cash/index.html.name: How does the Citi Custom Cash 5% category work?
cards/citi-custom-cash/index.html.acceptedAnswer: Each billing cycle, Citi automatically identifies your top eligible spending category and gives you 5% back on up to $500 in that category. No activation, no sign-ups. If you spend $600 on dining in a month, you earn 5% on $500 ($25) and 1% on the remaining $100 ($1).

cards/citi-custom-cash/index.html.name: What categories qualify for the 5%?
cards/citi-custom-cash/index.html.acceptedAnswer: Qualifying categories include: restaurants, supermarkets, gas stations, drugstores, fitness clubs, home improvement stores, online purchases, travel, and more. The card automatically picks whichever category you spent the most in each billing cycle.

cards/citi-custom-cash/index.html.name: Is the Custom Cash better than the Freedom Flex?
cards/citi-custom-cash/index.html.acceptedAnswer: Depends. Custom Cash gives a guaranteed 5% on your top category every month with no effort. Freedom Flex gives 5% on rotating categories (which you have to activate) plus 3% on dining and drugstores. If you like set-it-and-forget-it, go Custom Cash. If you track rotating categories and want 3% ongoing on dining, go Freedom Flex.

cards/citi-custom-cash/index.html.name: Can I have both Citi Custom Cash and Citi Double Cash?
cards/citi-custom-cash/index.html.acceptedAnswer: Yes, and it's a great combo. Use Custom Cash for your top monthly category (5%) and Double Cash for everything else (2%). Together, they cover your spending at 2-5% with no annual fees on either card.

cards/citi-custom-cash/index.html.name: What happens if I spend less than $500 in my top category?
cards/citi-custom-cash/index.html.acceptedAnswer: You simply earn 5% on whatever you spend, up to $500. There's no minimum spend requirement for the 5% category. If your top category is $200, you earn 5% on $200 and 1% on everything else.

cards/citi-custom-cash/index.html.name: Is the $200 signup bonus easy to get?
cards/citi-custom-cash/index.html.acceptedAnswer: Relatively easy — $1,500 spend over 6 months works out to just $125/month. That's achievable with normal everyday spending. The 0% intro APR for 15 months also helps if you need to float a large purchase.

cards/chase-sapphire-preferred/index.htm.name: Is the Chase Sapphire Preferred worth the $95 annual fee?
cards/chase-sapphire-preferred/index.htm.acceptedAnswer: For most people who travel and dine out, yes. The $50 annual hotel credit alone covers more than half the fee, and the 5x travel / 3x dining rewards add up fast. The signup bonus alone (worth ~$750 in travel) covers the fee for ~7 years.

cards/chase-sapphire-preferred/index.htm.name: What are Chase Sapphire Preferred points worth?
cards/chase-sapphire-preferred/index.htm.acceptedAnswer: Points are worth 1.25¢ each when redeemed for travel through Chase Travel, or 1¢ for cash back. With Chase's transfer partners (Hyatt, United, Southwest, etc.), savvy redeemers regularly get 1.5–2¢+ per point.

cards/chase-sapphire-preferred/index.htm.name: What credit score do I need for the Chase Sapphire Preferred?
cards/chase-sapphire-preferred/index.htm.acceptedAnswer: Good to excellent credit (670+ FICO) is recommended. Chase also enforces the unwritten "5/24 rule" — if you've opened 5 or more credit cards from any issuer in the last 24 months, you'll likely be denied regardless of score.

cards/chase-sapphire-preferred/index.htm.name: Does the Chase Sapphire Preferred have foreign transaction fees?
cards/chase-sapphire-preferred/index.htm.acceptedAnswer: No — zero foreign transaction fees, making it a strong choice for international travel.

cards/chase-sapphire-preferred/index.htm.name: How does the Sapphire Preferred compare to the Reserve?
cards/chase-sapphire-preferred/index.htm.acceptedAnswer: The Reserve ($545 AF) adds airport lounge access, $300 annual travel credit, and 1.5¢/point redemption. The Preferred ($95) is a better value unless you fly enough to use the lounges (~10+ flights/year) and use the full $300 credit.

cards/chase-sapphire-preferred/index.htm.name: Can I downgrade the Sapphire Preferred later?
cards/chase-sapphire-preferred/index.htm.acceptedAnswer: Yes. After year 1, you can downgrade product-change to Chase Freedom Unlimited or Freedom Flex (no AF), keeping your account history. You can't upgrade back without a new application though.

cards/amazon-prime-visa-signature/index..name: Is the Amazon Prime Visa worth it if I already pay for Prime?
cards/amazon-prime-visa-signature/index..acceptedAnswer: Yes — there's no additional annual fee beyond your Prime membership ($139/yr). The 5% back on Amazon purchases effectively reduces the cost of everything you buy. If you spend $200+/month on Amazon, you're earning $10+/month = $120+/yr, which nearly covers Prime itself.

cards/amazon-prime-visa-signature/index..name: What happens if I cancel my Prime membership?
cards/amazon-prime-visa-signature/index..acceptedAnswer: The card reverts to the Amazon Visa with 3% back on Amazon instead of 5%. You keep all other earning rates. You won't lose the card, just the Prime bonus rate.

cards/amazon-prime-visa-signature/index..name: Does the 5% back at Whole Foods include everything?
cards/amazon-prime-visa-signature/index..acceptedAnswer: Yes — almost everything at Whole Foods qualifies for 5% back. This includes groceries, prepared foods, and supplements. Gift cards and alcohol may be excluded depending on local laws.

cards/amazon-prime-visa-signature/index..name: How does this compare to the Citi Custom Cash for Amazon?
cards/amazon-prime-visa-signature/index..acceptedAnswer: Citi Custom Cash gives 5% on your top spending category (up to $500/month). If Amazon is your top category, you get 5% with no Prime requirement. But Custom Cash has a $500/month cap, while the Amazon Prime Visa gives 5% on unlimited Amazon spend. Heavy Amazon shoppers should get both.

cards/amazon-prime-visa-signature/index..name: Can I use rewards for anything besides Amazon?
cards/amazon-prime-visa-signature/index..acceptedAnswer: Yes — you can redeem for statement credits, gift cards, travel through Chase, or transfer to airline/hotel partners if you also have a Chase Sapphire card. Amazon checkout redemption is the easiest, but Chase Ultimate Rewards transfer can be more valuable (1.25–1.5¢/point).

cards/amazon-prime-visa-signature/index..name: What about Prime Day — does the card offer extra rewards?
cards/amazon-prime-visa-signature/index..acceptedAnswer: Sometimes Amazon runs bonus offers for Prime Visa cardholders during Prime Day (e.g., extra 2% back or statement credits). These vary by year and aren't guaranteed, but Prime Day is generally the best time to max out your 5% rate.

cards/barclays-uber-pro/index.html.name: Is the Barclays Uber Pro Card worth getting?
cards/barclays-uber-pro/index.html.acceptedAnswer: If you spend $200+/month on Uber rides and Uber Eats, absolutely. The 7% back on Uber is the highest rideshare reward rate available. The Uber One credit alone ($120/yr) makes this a no-brainer for regular users. Even occasional users benefit since there's no annual fee.

cards/barclays-uber-pro/index.html.name: How does the 7% cash back on Uber work?
cards/barclays-uber-pro/index.html.acceptedAnswer: You earn 7% cash back on Uber rides and Uber Eats purchases, credited as Uber Cash to your Uber account. The 5% rate applies to Uber rides specifically — so if you use both Uber Eats and rides, you're earning 7% on the food delivery and 5% on the rides.

cards/barclays-uber-pro/index.html.name: What is UberVIP status?
cards/barclays-uber-pro/index.html.acceptedAnswer: UberVIP gives you priority matching with top-rated drivers in select cities. It's not available everywhere, and the benefit is modest compared to the cash-back rewards. Don't get the card just for UberVIP.

cards/barclays-uber-pro/index.html.name: Can I use Uber Cash for anything besides rides and food?
cards/barclays-uber-pro/index.html.acceptedAnswer: Yes — Uber Cash can be used for rides, Uber Eats orders, and Uber package delivery. It cannot be withdrawn as cash or applied to your credit card balance.

cards/barclays-uber-pro/index.html.name: How does this compare to the Amex Gold for food delivery?
cards/barclays-uber-pro/index.html.acceptedAnswer: Amex Gold gives 4x points on dining worldwide (including Uber Eats), but the Uber Pro gives a flat 7% on Uber Eats specifically. If you eat out at restaurants more than you order delivery, the Gold is better. If Uber Eats is your primary delivery, the Uber Pro is better.

cards/barclays-uber-pro/index.html.name: Does the Uber One credit apply automatically?
cards/barclays-uber-pro/index.html.acceptedAnswer: Yes — if you're an Uber One member, you'll receive a $9.99 monthly statement credit for your membership fee. If you're not a member, you can sign up and the credit covers the cost entirely.

cards/bofa-customized-cash-rewards/index.name: How does the BofA Customized Cash Rewards choice category work?
cards/bofa-customized-cash-rewards/index.acceptedAnswer: You pick one of six categories for 3%: gas, online shopping, dining, travel, drugstores, or home improvement. You can change it once per calendar month online or in the app. If you never change it, it stays on your previous selection. The 2% on groceries and wholesale clubs is always active.

cards/bofa-customized-cash-rewards/index.name: What is the BofA Preferred Rewards boost?
cards/bofa-customized-cash-rewards/index.acceptedAnswer: If you have $20K+ in a BofA checking/savings/investment account, you get a 25% rewards bonus (Gold tier). $50K+ = 50% bonus (Platinum). $100K+ = 75% bonus (Platinum Honors). This turns the 3% into 3.75%, 4.5%, or 5.25%. With Platinum Honors, you're earning 5.25% on your choice category — rivaling dedicated 5% cards with no annual fee.

cards/bofa-customized-cash-rewards/index.name: Is the Customized Cash Rewards better than the Citi Custom Cash?
cards/bofa-customized-cash-rewards/index.acceptedAnswer: For BofA banking customers with $100K+ in assets: absolutely. The 5.25% (3% × 1.75x) on your choice category beats Custom Cash's 5% — and there's no $500/month cap. For everyone else, Custom Cash gives a cleaner 5% on your top category with no asset requirements. If you don't BofA bank, skip this card.

cards/bofa-customized-cash-rewards/index.name: Can I really change the 3% category every month?
cards/bofa-customized-cash-rewards/index.acceptedAnswer: Yes, once per calendar month. Some people switch monthly — online shopping for holiday months, gas for summer road trips, dining for summer dining out. It's flexibility that most category cards don't offer.

cards/bofa-customized-cash-rewards/index.name: Does the 2% on groceries include Walmart and Target?
cards/bofa-customized-cash-rewards/index.acceptedAnswer: No. Like most cards, standalone supermarkets code as groceries. Walmart, Target, and warehouse clubs like Costco code differently. However, the 2% on wholesale clubs does cover Costco and Sam's Club — making this one of the few cards that earns bonus at warehouse clubs.

cards/bofa-customized-cash-rewards/index.name: Is the signup bonus worth it?
cards/bofa-customized-cash-rewards/index.acceptedAnswer: The $200 bonus after $1,000 spend in 90 days is decent for a no-annual-fee card. That's effectively 20% back on your first $1,000. After the bonus, ongoing value depends on your spending and whether you qualify for the Preferred Rewards boost.

cards/amex-blue-cash-preferred/index.htm.name: Is the Amex Blue Cash Preferred worth the $95 annual fee?
cards/amex-blue-cash-preferred/index.htm.acceptedAnswer: If you spend $400+/month at U.S. supermarkets, yes. At $400/mo, you earn $288/year in grocery cash back alone (6% on $4,800). Subtract the $95 AF and you're netting $193. Add gas/transit/streaming rewards and you're well into positive territory. Below $150/mo in groceries, the math flips — consider the no-AF Blue Cash Everyday instead.

cards/amex-blue-cash-preferred/index.htm.name: What counts as a "U.S. supermarket" for the 6%?
cards/amex-blue-cash-preferred/index.htm.acceptedAnswer: Standalone grocery stores like Kroger, Safeway, Publix, Whole Foods, and Trader Joe's. Superstores like Walmart, Target, Costco, and Sam's Club do NOT count. The $6,000 annual cap applies to the grocery category; after that, groceries earn 1%.

cards/amex-blue-cash-preferred/index.htm.name: How does the streaming 6% cash back work?
cards/amex-blue-cash-preferred/index.htm.acceptedAnswer: You earn 6% on eligible U.S. streaming subscriptions: Netflix, Hulu, Spotify, Disney+, Amazon Prime, Apple TV+, and more. There's no annual cap on streaming. This alone can net $50–$100/year if you have 3–5 subscriptions.

cards/amex-blue-cash-preferred/index.htm.name: Is the Blue Cash Preferred better than the Amex Gold for groceries?
cards/amex-blue-cash-preferred/index.htm.acceptedAnswer: BCP gives straight 6% cash back on up to $6K/yr. Gold gives 4x points on up to $25K/yr. If you value Amex points at 1.5¢ each, Gold gives an effective 6% but only if you transfer points to partners. For pure cash back in your pocket? BCP wins. For travel rewards? Gold wins.

cards/amex-blue-cash-preferred/index.htm.name: What happens after the $6,000 grocery cap?
cards/amex-blue-cash-preferred/index.htm.acceptedAnswer: Grocery spend above $6,000/year drops from 6% to 1%. If you spend more than $500/month on groceries, track your spend — beyond $6K, consider switching to a card like the Citi Custom Cash for the overage.

cards/amex-blue-cash-preferred/index.htm.name: Does the Blue Cash Preferred have foreign transaction fees?
cards/amex-blue-cash-preferred/index.htm.acceptedAnswer: No — Amex removed the foreign transaction fee on BCP. You can use it abroad for groceries and earn 1% (international supermarkets won't code as U.S. supermarkets for the 6% rate).

cards/chase-sapphire-reserve/index.html.name: Is the Chase Sapphire Reserve worth the $550 annual fee?
cards/chase-sapphire-reserve/index.html.acceptedAnswer: If you use the $300 travel credit and fly enough to use Priority Pass lounges, the effective fee drops to ~$0–$100. The 10x points on Chase Travel bookings and 1.5¢/point redemption value make it elite for heavy travelers. But if you barely travel, it's an expensive paperweight.

cards/chase-sapphire-reserve/index.html.name: How does the Sapphire Reserve compare to the Preferred?
cards/chase-sapphire-reserve/index.html.acceptedAnswer: Reserve gives 10x on Chase Travel vs 5x, 1.5¢/point vs 1.25¢, Priority Pass lounges, and $300 travel credit. Preferred costs $550 less per year. If you travel 6+ times/year and use lounges, Reserve wins. Otherwise, Preferred is the better value.

cards/chase-sapphire-reserve/index.html.name: What are Chase Sapphire Reserve points worth?
cards/chase-sapphire-reserve/index.html.acceptedAnswer: 1.5¢ each when redeemed for travel through Chase, or 1¢ for cash back. Transfer partners like Hyatt, United, and Singapore Airlines can yield 2–3¢+ per point for savvy redeemers.

cards/chase-sapphire-reserve/index.html.name: Can I downgrade the Sapphire Reserve?
cards/chase-sapphire-reserve/index.html.acceptedAnswer: Yes, you can product-change to Chase Sapphire Preferred, Freedom Flex, or Freedom Unlimited. You'll lose lounge access and the travel credit, but avoid the $550 AF. Note: you can't upgrade back without a new application.

cards/chase-sapphire-reserve/index.html.name: Does the $300 travel credit work automatically?
cards/chase-sapphire-reserve/index.html.acceptedAnswer: Yes. It credits automatically for qualifying travel purchases (airlines, hotels, car rentals, transit). No enrollment or portal booking required — just make the purchase and the credit posts within a few days.

cards/chase-sapphire-reserve/index.html.name: How does Priority Pass work with the Reserve?
cards/chase-sapphire-reserve/index.html.acceptedAnswer: You get Priority Pass Select membership with unlimited lounge visits for yourself and unlimited free guests. Most other premium cards charge $27+ per guest. This alone can be worth $500+/year if you travel with companions.

cards/discover-it-cash-back/index.html.name: How does the Discover it Cashback Match work?
cards/discover-it-cash-back/index.html.acceptedAnswer: In your first 12 billing cycles, Discover matches ALL the cash back you've earned — dollar for dollar. If you earn $300 in cash back, they give you another $300 at the end of the year. That makes the rotating 5% categories effectively 10% in year one. After year one, you earn the regular rates only.

cards/discover-it-cash-back/index.html.name: What are the 2026 rotating categories?
cards/discover-it-cash-back/index.html.acceptedAnswer: Discover typically announces categories quarterly. Recent categories include: Q1 grocery stores, Q2 gas stations & Uber, Q3 restaurants, Q4 Amazon & Target. You must activate each quarter at Discover.com or in the app — if you forget, you only earn 1%.

cards/discover-it-cash-back/index.html.name: Is Discover it Cash Back better than Chase Freedom Flex?
cards/discover-it-cash-back/index.html.acceptedAnswer: Year one: Yes, Discover is better because of the Cashback Match (effectively doubles everything). Year two and beyond: Freedom Flex is better because it has 3% ongoing on dining and drugstores, while Discover drops to 1% on non-rotating categories. If you're choosing one, get both — use Discover in year one, then switch to Freedom Flex.

cards/discover-it-cash-back/index.html.name: Can I have both the Discover it Cash Back and Discover it Miles?
cards/discover-it-cash-back/index.html.acceptedAnswer: No. Discover typically only allows one card per person. If you have the Miles card, you'd need to close it before applying for Cash Back, or product-change (which is a Discover-internal process — call them).

cards/discover-it-cash-back/index.html.name: Where is Discover not accepted?
cards/discover-it-cash-back/index.html.acceptedAnswer: Discover has closed the acceptance gap significantly and is now accepted at 99% of US merchants that take credit cards. The main holdouts are some small businesses and international merchants in certain countries. Costco accepts Discover but not Amex in most locations.

cards/discover-it-cash-back/index.html.name: Is the first-year match really unlimited?
cards/discover-it-cash-back/index.html.acceptedAnswer: Yes — there's no cap on the Cashback Match. If you somehow earn $1,000 in cash back in your first year, Discover gives you another $1,000. The only cap is on the rotating 5% categories ($1,500/quarter max at 5%), but the match applies to ALL earnings including 1% on everyday spending.

cards/ihg-one-rewards-premier/index.html.name: Is the IHG Premier worth the $99 annual fee?
cards/ihg-one-rewards-premier/index.html.acceptedAnswer: Yes, easily — if you stay at IHG hotels even once a year. The free night award (worth ~$150-200) and $100 statement credit together are worth $250-300, dwarfing the $99 fee. You're netting $150-200/year minimum just from the annual benefits.

cards/ihg-one-rewards-premier/index.html.name: How does the 4th night free on award stays work?
cards/ihg-one-rewards-premier/index.html.acceptedAnswer: When you book an award stay of 4 or more nights at an IHG property using points, every 4th night is free (0 points required for that night). On a 4-night stay, you pay for 3 nights. On an 8-night stay, you pay for 6. This can save 25% on longer stays.

cards/ihg-one-rewards-premier/index.html.name: How much are IHG points worth?
cards/ihg-one-rewards-premier/index.html.acceptedAnswer: ~0.5¢ each, making the 26x rate on IHG stays equivalent to 13% back. That sounds great until you realize 175,000 points ≈ $875 in free nights. The points are most valuable at lower-tier properties like Holiday Inn Express where a night can cost 15,000-25,000 points.

cards/ihg-one-rewards-premier/index.html.name: Is the free night award really worth $200?
cards/ihg-one-rewards-premier/index.html.acceptedAnswer: You can redeem it for any IHG hotel that costs up to 40,000 points per night. Many Holiday Inn Express and even some Crowne Plaza properties fall in this range. If you use it at a $200/night property (common in major cities), the value is $200. If you apply it to a $150 Holiday Inn, the value is $150.

cards/ihg-one-rewards-premier/index.html.name: How does this compare to the Hyatt card for hotel stays?
cards/ihg-one-rewards-premier/index.html.acceptedAnswer: Hyatt points are worth ~1.5¢ each vs IHG's ~0.5¢ each, making Hyatt's earning more valuable per point. However, IHG has far more properties (6,000+ vs 1,300+), so availability is better. If you can find Hyatt properties where you travel, the Chase Hyatt card is better. If you need broad coverage, IHG wins.

cards/ihg-one-rewards-premier/index.html.name: Can I combine the free night with the 4th night free?
cards/ihg-one-rewards-premier/index.html.acceptedAnswer: Yes! Book a 4-night award stay, and the 4th night is free. Then use your annual free night certificate for one of the paid nights. This combination can make a 4-night stay cost just 2 nights worth of points plus one certificate — incredibly efficient.

cards/chase-freedom-flex/index.html.name: How do the Chase Freedom Flex rotating categories work?
cards/chase-freedom-flex/index.html.acceptedAnswer: Each quarter, Chase announces new 5% categories (e.g., Q1: groceries and fitness; Q2: gas and Lyft; Q3: dining and PayPal; Q4: Amazon and Target). You must activate online or in the app each quarter. You earn 5% on up to $1,500 in combined purchases across the quarter's categories — that's up to $75 cash back per quarter, $300/year.

cards/chase-freedom-flex/index.html.name: Is the Chase Freedom Flex better than the old Chase Freedom?
cards/chase-freedom-flex/index.html.acceptedAnswer: Yes. The Flex added 3% on dining and drugstores (ongoing, not rotating), cell phone protection, and no foreign transaction fees. The old Freedom only had 1% on non-rotating purchases. If you still have the old Freedom, call Chase and ask to product-change to the Flex — same account, better rewards.

cards/chase-freedom-flex/index.html.name: Can I combine Freedom Flex with Chase Sapphire Preferred or Reserve?
cards/chase-freedom-flex/index.html.acceptedAnswer: Absolutely — and you should. Freedom Flex cash back converts to Chase Ultimate Rewards points (at 1¢ each) when you also hold a Sapphire card. This means your 5% and 3% earnings become 5x and 3x UR points, which you can transfer to Hyatt, United, Southwest, and 12+ other partners at 1.25–1.5¢ per point.

cards/chase-freedom-flex/index.html.name: What are the 2026 rotating categories for Freedom Flex?
cards/chase-freedom-flex/index.html.acceptedAnswer: Chase typically announces categories each quarter. Recent patterns: Q1 (Jan–Mar) = groceries/drugstores; Q2 (Apr–Jun) = gas/Lyft; Q3 (Jul–Sep) = dining/streaming; Q4 (Oct–Dec) = Amazon/Target/PayPal. Always verify on Chase's website and activate on day one of each quarter.

cards/chase-freedom-flex/index.html.name: Is the Freedom Flex worth it without activating categories?
cards/chase-freedom-flex/index.html.acceptedAnswer: Less so. Without 5% categories, you're getting 3% on dining and drugstores 1% on everything else. That's still decent for a no-AF card, but you're leaving $300/year on the table. Set a calendar reminder for quarterly activation.

cards/chase-freedom-flex/index.html.name: How does the Freedom Flex compare to the Discover it Cash Back?
cards/chase-freedom-flex/index.html.acceptedAnswer: Both offer 5% rotating categories. Key differences: Flex has 3% ongoing on dining/drugstores (Discover has 1%), no foreign transaction fees (Discover is accepted in fewer places abroad), and pairs with Chase UR ecosystem. Discover has the Cashback Match (doubles all first-year earnings) making it better in year one. Flex is better long-term.

cards/us-bank-altitude-go/index.html.name: Is the US Bank Altitude Go worth it?
cards/us-bank-altitude-go/index.html.acceptedAnswer: If you spend $400+/month on dining, yes. The 4x rate on dining is the best no-annual-fee rate available, and the 2x on groceries/gas/streaming/travel rounds out a solid everyday card. The $30 streaming credit and 0% intro APR are cherries on top.

cards/us-bank-altitude-go/index.html.name: What are Altitude Go points worth?
cards/us-bank-altitude-go/index.html.acceptedAnswer: 1¢ each for cash back (statement credit, direct deposit). Unlike the Altitude Reserve, Go points cannot be transferred to travel partners. This makes the Go a pure cash-back card dressed up as a points card.

cards/us-bank-altitude-go/index.html.name: How does the Altitude Go compare to the Capital One SavorOne?
cards/us-bank-altitude-go/index.html.acceptedAnswer: SavorOne offers 3% on dining and 3% on groceries (vs 4% and 2%). SavorOne wins on groceries, Go wins on dining. SavorOne has 8% on Capital One Entertainment. Go has the $30 streaming credit. Both are no-AF — pick based on whether you spend more on dining (Go) or groceries (SavorOne).

cards/us-bank-altitude-go/index.html.name: What is the $30 streaming credit?
cards/us-bank-altitude-go/index.html.acceptedAnswer: US Bank gives you a $30 annual credit for streaming subscriptions (Netflix, Hulu, Spotify, etc.) charged to the card. It's reimbursed as a statement credit. If you subscribe to any 2-3 streaming services, you'll easily max this out.

cards/us-bank-altitude-go/index.html.name: Is the US Bank Altitude Go hard to get approved for?
cards/us-bank-altitude-go/index.html.acceptedAnswer: US Bank is pickier than Capital One but less strict than Chase. They look at recent inquiries and may deny you if you've opened 3+ cards in the past 6 months. Pre-qualify on their website first for a soft-pull check.

cards/us-bank-altitude-go/index.html.name: Can I upgrade to the Altitude Reserve later?
cards/us-bank-altitude-go/index.html.acceptedAnswer: You can product-change from Go to Reserve (subject to approval). The Reserve has a $400 annual fee but gives 4.5x on travel and mobile wallet purchases plus Priority Pass. Only worth it if you travel heavily.

cards/citi-strata-premier/index.html.name: Is the Citi Strata Premier worth the $95 annual fee?
cards/citi-strata-premier/index.html.acceptedAnswer: If you spend $1,000+/month across travel, dining, and gas, yes. The 3x rate on those categories earns roughly $540/year in rewards on $1,500/mo spend. Subtract the $95 AF and net the $100 hotel credit, and you're at $545 net value. Without the hotel credit use, it's still $445 net — solid for a $95 card.

cards/citi-strata-premier/index.html.name: What are Citi ThankYou Points worth?
cards/citi-strata-premier/index.html.acceptedAnswer: 1¢ each for cash back or statement credit. 1.5¢ each when redeemed for travel through Citi Travel. 1.5–2.5¢ each when transferred to partners like JetBlue, Virgin Atlantic, or Wyndham. The transfer partners aren't as strong as Chase or Amex, but they're workable for flexible travelers.

cards/citi-strata-premier/index.html.name: How does the Strata Premier compare to Chase Sapphire Preferred?
cards/citi-strata-premier/index.html.acceptedAnswer: Both cost $95/year. CSP gives 5x on Chase Travel, 3x on dining/streaming/online groceries, and stronger travel insurance (primary rental car coverage, trip delay). Strata gives 3x on a broader set of categories (air, hotels, gas, restaurants, EV charging) but weaker insurance and transfer partners. CSP wins on ecosystem and insurance; Strata wins on breadth of 3x categories.

cards/citi-strata-premier/index.html.name: What is the $100 annual hotel credit?
cards/citi-strata-premier/index.html.acceptedAnswer: Each card anniversary year, you get a $100 statement credit for hotel bookings through Citi Travel (partnered with Booking.com). Book a $100+ hotel stay and the credit covers it. If you stay in hotels at least once a year, this effectively reduces the annual fee to $0 or less.

cards/citi-strata-premier/index.html.name: Is the Priority Pass membership useful?
cards/citi-strata-premier/index.html.acceptedAnswer: Marginally. You get 1 free lounge visit per year (cardholder only), then $32 per visit. Compared to the Venture X's unlimited visits with 2 guests, this is a teaser. Don't factor it heavily into your decision.

cards/citi-strata-premier/index.html.name: Can I combine Strata Premier with the Citi Double Cash?
cards/citi-strata-premier/index.html.acceptedAnswer: Yes — and it's a great pairing. Use Strata for travel/dining/gas (3x) and Double Cash for everything else (2%). Plus, having both cards lets you convert Double Cash earnings into ThankYou Points for travel transfers, unlocking 1.5–2+¢ per point redemption.

cards/bilt-mastercard/index.html.name: How does the Bilt Mastercard earn points on rent?
cards/bilt-mastercard/index.html.acceptedAnswer: You link your rent payment in the Bilt app. Bilt sends a check or ACH to your landlord on your behalf, and you earn 1x point per dollar of rent. You pay Bilt back from your linked bank account. No transaction fees, no landlord involvement needed.

cards/bilt-mastercard/index.html.name: Is the Bilt Mastercard really free with no annual fee?
cards/bilt-mastercard/index.html.acceptedAnswer: Yes — $0 annual fee, no foreign transaction fees. Bilt makes money from interchange fees and their rewards marketplace. The catch: you must use the card for 5 transactions per statement period (Rent Day counts) to earn rent points.

cards/bilt-mastercard/index.html.name: How much are Bilt points worth?
cards/bilt-mastercard/index.html.acceptedAnswer: 1¢ each for cash back or statement credit, ~1.4¢ through travel partners. Transfer partners include Hyatt, United, American Airlines, and others. The Hyatt transfer is particularly valuable — Bilt to Hyatt points can be worth 1.5–2¢ each.

cards/bilt-mastercard/index.html.name: What happens if my landlord doesn't accept Bilt?
cards/bilt-mastercard/index.html.acceptedAnswer: Bilt sends a physical check or ACH transfer — no landlord signup required. They even include a pre-filled check template. In practice, 95%+ of landlords can receive Bilt payments without any effort on their part.

cards/bilt-mastercard/index.html.name: Does Bilt have a catch?
cards/bilt-mastercard/index.html.acceptedAnswer: The main catch is the 5-transaction requirement per billing cycle to earn rent points. The card also has limited dining/travel bonuses compared to dedicated category cards. And you need to pay your rent through Bilt's system rather than just swiping the card.

cards/bilt-mastercard/index.html.name: Can I use the Bilt Mastercard for regular purchases?
cards/bilt-mastercard/index.html.acceptedAnswer: Absolutely. Beyond rent (1x), it earns 3x on dining, 2x on travel, and 1x on everything else. That's competitive with many $95+ annual fee cards, especially for dining-heavy spenders.

cards/amex-platinum/index.html.name: Is the Amex Platinum worth the $695 annual fee?
cards/amex-platinum/index.html.acceptedAnswer: Only if you use the credits. The $1,484+ in annual credits can offset the fee, but many are fragmented ($15/mo Uber, $20/mo digital, etc.) and require active redemption. If you fly 8+ times/year and use Centurion lounges + hotel benefits, it's excellent. If not, the math doesn't work.

cards/amex-platinum/index.html.name: What's the real value of Amex Platinum credits?
cards/amex-platinum/index.html.acceptedAnswer: Face value is ~$1,484/yr, but real value depends on your lifestyle. Uber credits expire monthly, digital credits require specific subscriptions, and the Saks credit is semi-annual. Most cardholders realistically use $700–$900 of credits, making the effective AF $0–$200.

cards/amex-platinum/index.html.name: How do Centurion Lounges compare to Priority Pass?
cards/amex-platinum/index.html.acceptedAnswer: Centurion Lounges are significantly better — full hot buffets, craft cocktails, spa services. But they're only in ~15 U.S. airports. Priority Pass has 1,400+ locations globally but most are basic. Having both is the power move.

cards/amex-platinum/index.html.name: Amex Platinum vs Chase Sapphire Reserve?
cards/amex-platinum/index.html.acceptedAnswer: Platinum has better lounges (Centurion) and more credits ($1,484 vs $450). Reserve has better earning rates (3–10x vs 1x on most purchases), is $145 less expensive, and has stronger travel insurance. Platinum is a lifestyle card; Reserve is a rewards card.

cards/amex-platinum/index.html.name: Are Membership Rewards points from the Platinum worth it?
cards/amex-platinum/index.html.acceptedAnswer: The earning rates are unremarkable (5x flights, 1x everything else). The value comes from transfer partners: Aeroplan, ANA, Avianca, Delta, and hotel programs can yield 2–4¢/point. If you don't transfer, stick to the portal (1¢/point baseline).

cards/amex-platinum/index.html.name: Can I downgrade the Amex Platinum?
cards/amex-platinum/index.html.acceptedAnswer: You can't product-change from a charge card to a credit card in Amex's system. You'd need to close the Platinum and apply separately. Consider the Amex Gold ($325) if you want to stay in the ecosystem at lower cost.

cards/citi-premier/index.html.name: Is the Citi Premier worth the $95 annual fee?
cards/citi-premier/index.html.acceptedAnswer: Easily — if you use the 3x categories. Spend $1,000/month across gas, groceries, and dining and you're earning 36,000 ThankYou Points per year ($360+ in travel value). The $100 annual hotel credit covers most of the fee, leaving just net $5/yr. The signup bonus alone ($600 in travel) covers the fee for 6+ years.

cards/citi-premier/index.html.name: How does the Citi Premier differ from the Citi Strata Premier?
cards/citi-premier/index.html.acceptedAnswer: The Citi Strata Premier ($400/yr) is the premium version — it adds airport lounge access (Priority Pass), a $250 annual travel credit, and a higher signup bonus. The regular Citi Premier ($95/yr) is the better value for most people. Only upgrade to Strata if you use airport lounges regularly.

cards/citi-premier/index.html.name: What are Citi ThankYou Points worth?
cards/citi-premier/index.html.acceptedAnswer: 1¢ each for cash back, gift cards, or statement credits. 1.25¢ each when redeemed for travel through Citi Travel. Transfers to airline partners (JetBlue, Singapore Airlines, Virgin Atlantic, etc.) can yield 1.5–2¢+ per point. The Premier is the key to unlocking transfer partners — without it, ThankYou Points from the Double Cash are worth only 1¢ each.

cards/citi-premier/index.html.name: Can I combine Citi Premier points with Citi Double Cash?
cards/citi-premier/index.html.acceptedAnswer: Yes! This is the power move. The Citi Double Cash earns 2x ThankYou Points on everything. With the Premier, those points become transferable to airline/hotel partners at 1¢+ each instead of being locked to 1¢ cash back. The combo is called "CitiDoublePremier" and it's one of the best point-earning setups available.

cards/citi-premier/index.html.name: How does gas station 3x work with EV charging?
cards/citi-premier/index.html.acceptedAnswer: The 3x rate applies to both traditional gas stations and EV charging stations. This is rare — most cards only bonus gas, not EV charging. If you drive an EV and charge at public stations, the Premier is one of the best cards for that spend category.

cards/citi-premier/index.html.name: What happens to my points if I downgrade?
cards/citi-premier/index.html.acceptedAnswer: If you downgrade the Citi Premier to the Citi Custom Cash or Double Cash, you keep all accumulated ThankYou Points. However, you lose the ability to transfer points to travel partners — they revert to 1¢ cash value only. Transfer your points to partners before downgrading.

cards/amex-blue-cash-everyday/index.html.name: Is the Amex Blue Cash Everyday worth it?
cards/amex-blue-cash-everyday/index.html.acceptedAnswer: If you spend $200–$500/month at U.S. supermarkets, yes. At $300/month, you'd earn $108/year in grocery cash back alone. Add gas and online retail and you're looking at $200–$300+/year in total cash back with zero annual fee. It's the best no-AF grocery card if you don't want to track rotating categories.

cards/amex-blue-cash-everyday/index.html.name: What counts as "U.S. online retail" for the 3%?
cards/amex-blue-cash-everyday/index.html.acceptedAnswer: Online purchases from U.S. retailers not classified as supermarkets, gas stations, or travel. This includes Amazon, Target.com, Walmart.com, and most online stores. The $6,000/year cap means you earn 3% on up to $500/month of online shopping.

cards/amex-blue-cash-everyday/index.html.name: Blue Cash Everyday vs Blue Cash Preferred — which is right?
cards/amex-blue-cash-everyday/index.html.acceptedAnswer: BCP gives 6% on groceries for $95/year. BCE gives 3% on groceries for $0/year. Break-even: if you spend more than ~$160/month at U.S. supermarkets, BCP earns more after the fee. BCP also adds 6% streaming and 3% transit. If you're a light grocery spender or hate annual fees, BCE is the move.

cards/amex-blue-cash-everyday/index.html.name: Can I upgrade from Blue Cash Everyday to Blue Cash Preferred?
cards/amex-blue-cash-everyday/index.html.acceptedAnswer: Yes. After having the BCE for 12+ months, you can request a product change to the BCP. You'll start earning 6% on groceries, but you'll also incur the $95 annual fee. Amex sometimes offers upgrade bonuses (e.g., $150 statement credit) — watch for those.

cards/amex-blue-cash-everyday/index.html.name: Does the $6,000 annual cap apply to each category separately?
cards/amex-blue-cash-everyday/index.html.acceptedAnswer: Yes. The $6,000 cap is per category. You get $6K at supermarkets, $6K at gas stations, and $6K at online retail — each earning 3%. After each $6K cap, that category drops to 1%. For most people, the caps won't matter on gas and online retail, but heavy grocery spenders ($500+/mo) should track the supermarket cap.

cards/amex-blue-cash-everyday/index.html.name: How does the Blue Cash Everyday compare to the Citi Custom Cash?
cards/amex-blue-cash-everyday/index.html.acceptedAnswer: BCE gives 3% on groceries capped at $6K/yr. Custom Cash gives 5% on your top category capped at $500/mo spending. Custom Cash earns more on groceries up to $500/mo ($25/mo vs $15/mo), but BCE gives 3% on gas AND online retail too. If groceries are your only big category, Custom Cash wins. If you want broader 3% coverage, BCE wins.

cards/capital-one-savorone/index.html.name: Is the SavorOne really no annual fee?
cards/capital-one-savorone/index.html.acceptedAnswer: Yes, truly $0 annual fee forever. No foreign transaction fees either. Capital One makes money on interchange and interest from people who carry balances — but if you pay in full, it's completely free.

cards/capital-one-savorone/index.html.name: How does the SavorOne compare to the Amex Gold for dining?
cards/capital-one-savorone/index.html.acceptedAnswer: SavorOne gives 3% cash back on dining (no AF). Amex Gold gives 4x points on dining ($325 AF). If you value Amex points at 1.5¢ each, Gold earns 6% equivalent on dining — but you need to transfer points and pay $325/yr. SavorOne is the better pure cash back play for casual diners.

cards/capital-one-savorone/index.html.name: Is the 8% entertainment category real?
cards/capital-one-savorone/index.html.acceptedAnswer: Yes, but it's limited to specific purchases: concert tickets through Capital One Entertainment, streaming services, and live events. You won't get 8% at Ticketmaster or StubHub — only Capital One's own ticketing platform. Still, 3% on dining and groceries is where most of your value comes from.

cards/capital-one-savorone/index.html.name: What's the intro APR deal?
cards/capital-one-savorone/index.html.acceptedAnswer: 0% for 15 months on both purchases and balance transfers (3% BT fee). This makes the SavorOne one of the best no-AF cards for financing a large purchase or consolidating debt interest-free for over a year.

cards/capital-one-savorone/index.html.name: Can I combine SavorOne with a Venture X?
cards/capital-one-savorone/index.html.acceptedAnswer: Yes — and this is where it gets powerful. You can transfer SavorOne cash back as miles to a Venture X card (at a 1:1 ratio), effectively getting 3x–8x miles on dining, groceries, and entertainment that redeem at 1¢–2¢+ each.

cards/capital-one-savorone/index.html.name: Is the SavorOne hard to get approved for?
cards/capital-one-savorone/index.html.acceptedAnswer: Moderate. Capital One pre-qualifies with a soft pull, so check before applying. You'll typically need a 670+ FICO. They're more lenient than Chase but stricter than Discover.

cards/wells-fargo-active-cash/index.html.name: Is the Wells Fargo Active Cash better than the Citi Double Cash?
cards/wells-fargo-active-cash/index.html.acceptedAnswer: Nearly identical for rewards — both give 2% on everything. Active Cash has a $200 signup bonus (Double Cash has none) and 15 months 0% on purchases AND balance transfers (Double Cash is 18 months on BTs only, no purchase intro). Active Cash also includes cell phone protection. Long-term, they're equivalent. Short-term, Active Cash wins with the bonus.

cards/wells-fargo-active-cash/index.html.name: How does the 2% cash back work?
cards/wells-fargo-active-cash/index.html.acceptedAnswer: Simple: every purchase earns 2% back as cash rewards. No categories, no caps, no activation needed. You can redeem as a statement credit, direct deposit to a Wells Fargo account, or check. No minimum redemption threshold for statement credit.

cards/wells-fargo-active-cash/index.html.name: Should I get the Active Cash or the Wells Fargo Autograph?
cards/wells-fargo-active-cash/index.html.acceptedAnswer: Both are no-AF cards from Wells Fargo. Active Cash gives flat 2% everywhere. Autograph gives 3x on dining, gas, transit, streaming, phone plans, and travel — but 1x on everything else. If you spend disproportionately on those 5 categories, Autograph wins. If your spend is spread out, Active Cash is simpler and often better.

cards/wells-fargo-active-cash/index.html.name: Is the cell phone protection good?
cards/wells-fargo-active-cash/index.html.acceptedAnswer: It covers damage and theft up to $600/claim with a $25 deductible (max $1,200/year). You must pay your cell phone bill with the card. At typical carrier insurance rates of $10–$15/month, this saves you $120–$180/year. Just make sure you set your phone bill to autopay on the Active Cash.

cards/wells-fargo-active-cash/index.html.name: Can I upgrade to the Wells Fargo Autograph later?
cards/wells-fargo-active-cash/index.html.acceptedAnswer: Yes, after 12+ months of good payment history, you can product-change to the Autograph or other Wells Fargo cards. You won't get the Autograph's signup bonus on a product change, though — that's only for new applications.

cards/wells-fargo-active-cash/index.html.name: Is the Wells Fargo Active Cash hard to get approved for?
cards/wells-fargo-active-cash/index.html.acceptedAnswer: Moderate. Wells Fargo usually wants a 670+ FICO score. They look at income and recent inquiries. The pre-qualification tool on their website uses a soft pull, so check there first. Approval is generally easier than Chase but slightly harder than Capital One.

cards/chase-ink-business-preferred/index.name: Do I need an LLC or corporation to get this card?
cards/chase-ink-business-preferred/index.acceptedAnswer: No. Chase considers any legitimate business activity — including sole proprietorships, freelancing, gig work, and side hustles. You can apply with your Social Security number as a sole prop. Just report your business income honestly. Having a registered business (LLC) may increase your approval odds and credit limit.

cards/chase-ink-business-preferred/index.name: Is the Ink Business Preferred worth it for a sole proprietor?
cards/chase-ink-business-preferred/index.acceptedAnswer: Absolutely, if you have legitimate business expenses. Even a freelance writer or rideshare driver likely spends on internet/phone (3x), shipping (3x for any packages), or advertising (3x for social media ads). The $8K/3mo signup spend is steep, but if you can put business expenses on it, the 100K points ($1,250+ in travel) is the best business card bonus available.

cards/chase-ink-business-preferred/index.name: How does the 3x on advertising work?
cards/chase-ink-business-preferred/index.acceptedAnswer: The 3x rate applies to social media advertising (Facebook, Instagram, Google Ads, etc.) and search engine advertising. This is huge for small businesses running online ads. If you spend $500/month on Facebook and Google Ads, that's 18,000 points/year ($225+ in travel value).

cards/chase-ink-business-preferred/index.name: Can I combine Ink points with Chase Sapphire points?
cards/chase-ink-business-preferred/index.acceptedAnswer: Yes — this is the real power. Ink Business Preferred earns Chase Ultimate Rewards points, the same currency as Chase Sapphire Preferred/Reserve. Combined with a Sapphire card, you can transfer points to 14 airline and hotel partners (Hyatt, United, Southwest, etc.) at full value. Without a Sapphire card, points are worth 1¢ each for cash back.

cards/chase-ink-business-preferred/index.name: What counts as "shipping" for the 3x category?
cards/chase-ink-business-preferred/index.acceptedAnswer: USPS, UPS, FedEx, DHL, and other shipping services qualify. This includes shipping supplies purchased from shipping providers. It does not include general office supplies or packaging materials bought from Amazon or office supply stores (those earn 1x).

cards/chase-ink-business-preferred/index.name: How does the Ink Business Preferred compare to the Amex Blue Business Plus?
cards/chase-ink-business-preferred/index.acceptedAnswer: Ink Preferred gives 3x on specific business categories (travel, shipping, internet/phone, advertising) and 1x on everything else. Amex Blue Business Plus gives 2x on everything (up to $50K/yr). Ink is better if you spend heavily in the 3x categories. Blue Business Plus is simpler if your spending is diverse and doesn't concentrate in those categories.

cards/amex-gold/index.html.name: Is the Amex Gold worth $325 annually?
cards/amex-gold/index.html.acceptedAnswer: If you actually use the credits ($424/yr face value), the card pays for itself before factoring rewards. The catch: most credits are split monthly/semi-annually so you have to remember to redeem them.

cards/amex-gold/index.html.name: What's the best way to use Membership Rewards points?
cards/amex-gold/index.html.acceptedAnswer: Transfer partners (Delta, ANA, Air France/KLM, Hilton, Marriott) typically yield 1.5–2.5¢/point. Avoid the gift card / pay-with-points-on-Amazon redemption — those are ~0.7¢/point.

cards/amex-gold/index.html.name: Are Amex Gold credits hard to use?
cards/amex-gold/index.html.acceptedAnswer: They're prorated monthly, which means you actively have to redeem them. People who set monthly Uber/Dunkin' reminders maximize value; people who don't end up leaving $200+/yr on the table.

cards/amex-gold/index.html.name: Does the Amex Gold count as a charge card?
cards/amex-gold/index.html.acceptedAnswer: It's technically a charge card with Pay Over Time — most spend must be paid in full each month, but you can opt eligible charges into a revolving plan with interest.

cards/amex-gold/index.html.name: How does the Amex Gold compare to the Chase Sapphire Preferred?
cards/amex-gold/index.html.acceptedAnswer: Gold is better for dining and groceries (4x vs 3x). Sapphire Preferred is cheaper ($95 vs $325) and has stronger travel insurance + transfer partners. Pick Gold if you spend $1K+/mo on restaurants/groceries.

cards/amex-gold/index.html.name: Is the Amex Gold worth it without using credits?
cards/amex-gold/index.html.acceptedAnswer: Less compelling. Strip out the $424 in coupon credits and you're paying $325/yr for 4x dining. Cards like Citi Custom Cash give 5% on a chosen category for $0 AF.

cards/wells-fargo-autograph/index.html.name: Is the Wells Fargo Autograph worth it?
cards/wells-fargo-autograph/index.html.acceptedAnswer: Yes — if you spend on dining, gas, transit, streaming, or phone plans. The 3x rate across 5 categories with no annual fee is one of the best no-fee setups available. The signup bonus ($330 value) is solid for a $0 AF card.

cards/wells-fargo-autograph/index.html.name: What are Wells Fargo points worth?
cards/wells-fargo-autograph/index.html.acceptedAnswer: Wells Fargo Go Far Rewards points are worth ~1.65¢ each when redeemed for travel through their portal, or 1¢ for cash back. With 11 transfer partners, you can potentially get 1.5–2¢+ per point on airline transfers, though the partner list isn't as deep as Chase or Amex.

cards/wells-fargo-autograph/index.html.name: How does the Autograph compare to the Chase Freedom Flex?
cards/wells-fargo-autograph/index.html.acceptedAnswer: Autograph gives consistent 3x on 5 categories with no activation needed. Freedom Flex gives 5% on rotating categories (up to $1,500/quarter) which can be more lucrative if you track the calendar, plus 3% on dining and drugstores. Autograph is set-and-forget; Freedom Flex is for people who like to optimize.

cards/wells-fargo-autograph/index.html.name: Does the Autograph count gas and transit separately?
cards/wells-fargo-autograph/index.html.acceptedAnswer: No — gas stations and transit (rideshare, buses, trains, parking, tolls) are combined into one "gas & transit" category. That means your Uber rides and gas fill-ups both earn 3x.

cards/wells-fargo-autograph/index.html.name: Is the cell phone protection good?
cards/wells-fargo-autograph/index.html.acceptedAnswer: It covers damage and theft up to $600 per claim ($1,200/year max, $25 deductible). You need to pay your monthly phone bill with the card to be eligible. This alone can save you $10-15/mo if you're paying for phone insurance through your carrier.

cards/wells-fargo-autograph/index.html.name: Can I downgrade or upgrade later?
cards/wells-fargo-autograph/index.html.acceptedAnswer: You can product-change to other Wells Fargo cards (like the Active Cash for a flat 2% setup). There's no penalty for upgrading/downgrading, but the Autograph is one of the best no-AF cards they offer.

cards/apple-card/index.html.name: Is the Apple Card a good credit card?
cards/apple-card/index.html.acceptedAnswer: It's the best no-fee card if you pay with Apple Pay at most places. The 2% on all Apple Pay purchases beats most flat-rate cards, and Daily Cash hitting your Apple Cash immediately is unmatched. But if you frequently use the physical card, you're earning just 1% — worse than basic 2% cards. It's a great companion card, not a primary card for non-Apple Pay users.

cards/apple-card/index.html.name: What is Daily Cash and how does it work?
cards/apple-card/index.html.acceptedAnswer: Daily Cash is Apple's term for cash back. It's deposited to your Apple Cash card every day — not monthly, not as a statement credit, but literally daily. You can spend it immediately via Apple Pay, send it to people, transfer it to your bank, or apply it to your Apple Card balance.

cards/apple-card/index.html.name: Does the Apple Card help build credit?
cards/apple-card/index.html.acceptedAnswer: Yes — it reports to all three credit bureaus (Equifax, Experian, TransUnion). The lack of late fees means a missed payment hurts your credit but doesn't add penalty charges. Goldman Sachs also offers a "path to Apple Card" program that helps you improve your credit to qualify.

cards/apple-card/index.html.name: What's the catch with no fees?
cards/apple-card/index.html.acceptedAnswer: No catch — there are truly no fees. No annual fee, no late fee, no over-limit fee, no foreign transaction fee. Goldman Sachs makes money from interest on carried balances and from Apple's partnership. This makes it one of the most consumer-friendly cards available, even if the rewards aren't category-leading.

cards/apple-card/index.html.name: Can I use the Apple Card without an iPhone?
cards/apple-card/index.html.acceptedAnswer: No. The Apple Card requires an iPhone running iOS 12.4 or later. You apply through the Wallet app, manage it in Wallet, and use Apple Pay for the 2–3% rates. Without an iPhone, you can't apply, manage, or maximize the card.

cards/apple-card/index.html.name: How does the Apple Card compare to the Citi Double Cash?
cards/apple-card/index.html.acceptedAnswer: Citi Double Cash gives 2% on everything (1% when you buy + 1% when you pay) regardless of payment method. Apple Card gives 2% only with Apple Pay and 1% with the physical card. If you Apple Pay everywhere, they're equivalent. If you ever use the physical card, Double Cash is better. Apple Card wins on UX and daily deposits; Double Cash wins on consistency.

cards/capital-one-quicksilver/index.html.name: Is the Capital One Quicksilver worth it?
cards/capital-one-quicksilver/index.html.acceptedAnswer: As a flat-rate cash-back card, yes. The 1.5% on everything with no annual fee and no category tracking is as simple as it gets. The $200 signup bonus and 0% intro APR seal the deal. But if you spend $500+/mo on groceries or dining, get a category card instead.

cards/capital-one-quicksilver/index.html.name: How does Quicksilver compare to Citi Double Cash?
cards/capital-one-quicksilver/index.html.acceptedAnswer: Both earn 2% effective (Double Cash: 1% + 1% when you pay; Quicksilver: 1.5% flat). Quicksilver gives a $200 signup bonus, 0% intro APR, and easier approval. Double Cash has the edge for pure ongoing rewards (2% vs 1.5%) and the ability to convert to ThankYou Points with a Citi Premier. For first-year value, Quicksilver wins. For long-term ceiling, Double Cash wins.

cards/capital-one-quicksilver/index.html.name: What credit score do I need for Quicksilver?
cards/capital-one-quicksilver/index.html.acceptedAnswer: Capital One is one of the most forgiving issuers. The Quicksilver has been approved for people with 630+ scores, and even lower with good income. Pre-qualify on their website for a soft-pull check before applying.

cards/capital-one-quicksilver/index.html.name: Is the 1.5% really enough?
cards/capital-one-quicksilver/index.html.acceptedAnswer: On $2,000/mo spending, that's $30/month or $360/year. A category card earning 3-5% on your top categories would earn more, but only if you bother to use the right card for each purchase. Quicksilver is the "never think about it" card.

cards/capital-one-quicksilver/index.html.name: Can I upgrade from QuicksilverOne to Quicksilver?
cards/capital-one-quicksilver/index.html.acceptedAnswer: Yes. Capital One regularly upgrades QuicksilverOne (which has a $39 annual fee) to Quicksilver (no annual fee) after 6-12 months of good payment history. If you have QuicksilverOne, call and ask for a product change.

cards/capital-one-quicksilver/index.html.name: Is the balance transfer offer good?
cards/capital-one-quicksilver/index.html.acceptedAnswer: The 0% for 15 months on purchases and balance transfers is competitive. The 3% balance transfer fee ($5 minimum) is standard. If you're carrying high-interest debt, the 15 months of 0% can save you hundreds in interest.

cards/citi-double-cash/index.html.name: How does the Citi Double Cash 2% actually work?
cards/citi-double-cash/index.html.acceptedAnswer: You earn 1% when you make a purchase, and another 1% when you pay it off. The "pay" half means you must pay your balance to get the full 2%. This effectively penalizes people who only make minimum payments — you'd only earn 1%.

cards/citi-double-cash/index.html.name: Is the Citi Double Cash better than a flat 2% card?
cards/citi-double-cash/index.html.acceptedAnswer: Effectively the same if you pay in full. The "1% + 1%" structure is a wash for full payers. Where Double Cash wins is the 18-month 0% BT offer, making it the top balance transfer card. Where it loses: many 2% cards (like Wells Fargo Active Cash) offer a signup bonus that Double Cash doesn't.

cards/citi-double-cash/index.html.name: Can I transfer Citi Double Cash rewards to travel partners?
cards/citi-double-cash/index.html.acceptedAnswer: Only if you also have a Citi Premier ($95 AF) or Citi Prestige. Then your Double Cash earnings convert to ThankYou Points (at 1¢ per point) and can transfer to 15+ airline and hotel partners. Without a premium Citi card, it's pure cash back only.

cards/citi-double-cash/index.html.name: What's the balance transfer deal?
cards/citi-double-cash/index.html.acceptedAnswer: 0% APR for 18 months on balance transfers with a 3% fee (min $5). After the intro period, the regular APR kicks in (18.99%–28.99%). This is one of the longest 0% BT offers available, making it excellent for debt consolidation.

cards/citi-double-cash/index.html.name: How does the Double Cash compare to the Wells Fargo Active Cash?
