merchant/subscription.html.acceptedAnswer: Amazon Prime membership ($139/yr) typically does not code as a streaming subscription — it codes as membership/retail. However, if you subscribe to Prime Video as a standalone service ($8.99/mo), that may qualify. The Amazon Prime Visa Signature gives 5% on all Amazon purchases including Prime.

merchant/subscription.html.name: Best no-annual-fee card for subscriptions?
merchant/subscription.html.acceptedAnswer: Citi Custom Cash gives 5% on your top spending category (up to $500/month) — if streaming is your top category, you earn 5% with no annual fee. Capital One SavorOne gives 3% on streaming with no cap and no annual fee.

merchant/subscription.html.name: Can I use multiple cards for different subscriptions?
merchant/subscription.html.acceptedAnswer: Yes. You can set different subscriptions to bill on different cards to maximize rewards. For example, use Blue Cash Preferred for Netflix/Hulu (6%), Amazon Prime Visa for Prime (5%), and Apple Card for Apple services (3% via Apple Pay).

merchant/travel.html.name: What is the best credit card for airlines?
merchant/travel.html.acceptedAnswer: Capital One Venture X offers 5x miles on flights, 10x hotels via Capital One Travel portal. Effective 9-18% value.

merchant/travel.html.name: Do direct airline purchases earn bonus?
merchant/travel.html.acceptedAnswer: Usually 1-2x unless co-branded airline card. Portal bookings unlock 5x+ multipliers.

merchant/travel.html.name: Best for hotels?
merchant/travel.html.acceptedAnswer: Capital One Venture X (10x via portal), Chase Sapphire Preferred (5x portal), Hilton/Marriott co-branded.

merchant/travel.html.name: Flexible travel cards vs airline-specific?
merchant/travel.html.acceptedAnswer: Flexible (Chase UR, Amex MR, Cap One miles) redeem anywhere; airline cards lock to one carrier.

merchant/fitness.html.name: Do gym memberships code as fitness or entertainment on credit cards?
merchant/fitness.html.acceptedAnswer: Most gym memberships code as 'health clubs/gym memberships' (MCC 7997) or 'merchandise' depending on the payment processor. Some cards specifically include gym memberships as a bonus category, while others count it under general purchases. Always check your card's category definitions.

merchant/fitness.html.name: What credit card gives the most cash back on fitness?
merchant/fitness.html.acceptedAnswer: The US Bank Cash+ card lets you choose 'gym memberships' as a 5% category. The BofA Customized Cash Rewards lets you pick 'dining' or 'online shopping' which covers many fitness apps. For Peloton specifically, cards with online shopping bonuses work best.

merchant/fitness.html.name: Does Peloton code as online shopping?
merchant/fitness.html.acceptedAnswer: Yes, Peloton equipment purchases and app subscriptions typically code as online shopping or miscellaneous retail, not as fitness. Cards with online shopping bonuses like the BofA Customized Cash Rewards (3% on online shopping) work well.

merchant/fitness.html.name: Can I use a fitness credit card for health insurance premiums?
merchant/fitness.html.acceptedAnswer: Health insurance premiums usually code as 'insurance' (MCC 6411), which falls under general purchases on most cards. However, some cards with health/wellness categories may cover it. Check your specific card terms.

merchant/fitness.html.name: Are fitness app subscriptions covered by streaming categories?
merchant/fitness.html.acceptedAnswer: Some fitness apps like Peloton, Apple Fitness+, and Nike Training Club code as streaming services and may earn streaming bonuses. Others code as general merchandise. Results vary by card and app — check your statement to see how each one codes.

merchant/groceries.html.name: Do Whole Foods and Trader Joe's count as groceries?
merchant/groceries.html.acceptedAnswer: Yes, both Whole Foods and Trader Joe's code as groceries/supermarkets on all major card networks. This means you'll earn bonus rewards with grocery category cards.

merchant/groceries.html.name: What is the best no-annual-fee grocery card?
merchant/groceries.html.acceptedAnswer: Citi Custom Cash offers 5% on your top spending category (groceries for most) with no annual fee. The catch: it is capped at $500/month in bonus spending.

merchant/groceries.html.name: Is the Amex Blue Cash Preferred worth the $95 fee?
merchant/groceries.html.acceptedAnswer: If you spend $500+/month on groceries, yes. 6% on $6,000/year = $360 back, minus $95 fee = $265 net. A free 3% card earns $180 on the same spend — the BCP wins by $85.

merchant/groceries.html.name: Does Costco count as a grocery store?
merchant/groceries.html.acceptedAnswer: Costco codes as a warehouse club, not a grocery store, for most cards. Chase and Amex warehouse club categories are separate. Check your card's terms.

merchant/groceries.html.name: How do I maximize Whole Foods rewards?
merchant/groceries.html.acceptedAnswer: Stack the Citi Custom Cash (5% on groceries) with Amazon Prime (5% at Whole Foods if you have Prime). Use the Prime card at Whole Foods and Custom Cash at other grocers.
